newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbek grain harvest at 2.9 mln T by Aug 4 - official.
newsitem.headline: Uzbek grain harvest at 2.9 mln T by Aug 4 - official.

text.p: Uzbekistan's grain harvest is near completion, with 2.866 million tonnes thrashed from 96 percent of areas sown to grains this year, a government official in the former Soviet republic said on Tuesday.

"As of August 4, grain was harvested from 96 percent of the total sown area. Now we have to gather grain from 56,000 hectares," an official from the macroeconomics and statistics ministry told Reuters on condition of anonymity.
A total of 1.49 million hectares were sown to grain this year, compared to 1.69 million in 1996.

The official said that grain yields so far averaged 2.21 tonnes per hectare but gave no comparison for year-ago levels. Around 2.70 million tonnes of grain had been harvested by the same date in 1996.

Officials in Uzbekistan, a Central Asian state with a population of 23 million people, have targeted grain output of 4.0 million tonnes this year, which would have meant achieving self-sufficiency in grain.
But just days before the end of the 1997 harvest, it appears that this year's crop is likely to fall well short of the official target.

Trade sources predict that Uzbekistan is likely to remain a large grain buyer this year, adding that last year, when the grain harvest totalled 3.54 million tonnes, Uzbekistan had to import about 1.6 million tonnes of wheat.
But the government official argued with this estimate.
"No grain imports are planned so far," he told Reuters.
